## Purpose and modeling strategy

This notebook develops a reproducible model for predicting `TARGET`, where a
value of 1 identifies an applicant with payment difficulty. The primary goal is
to maximize out-of-sample ROC AUC while keeping the process understandable,
computationally practical, and free from validation leakage.

Every candidate uses the same five stratified folds. Feature encoders,
imputation values, rare-category rules, and model parameters are learned from
the analysis portion of a fold and then applied to its assessment portion. This
means differences in model performance cannot be attributed to different data
splits or to information leaking from assessment rows into preprocessing.

::: {.callout-important title="Primary modeling rule"}
All learned preprocessing must occur inside cross-validation. Fitting imputation
or category rules on the complete training dataset before cross-validation would
allow assessment-fold information to influence model development and could
inflate the reported AUC.
:::

The notebook compares a null model, elastic-net logistic regression, a pruned
decision tree, a random forest, and gradient-boosted trees. ROC AUC is the main
selection measure. PR AUC is included because the event class is uncommon, and
Brier score is included to assess probability error.

## 1. Setup and reproducibility controls

```{r}
#| label: setup

source("Scripts/data_preparation.R")
source("Scripts/modeling_pipeline.R")

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(readr)

check_modeling_packages()

SEED <- 6812L
CV_FOLDS <- 5L
NTHREAD <- 4L

# Supplemental credit-history features generally improve AUC. Their aggregated
# application-level form is cached after the first run because the source files
# exceed 2 GB in total.
USE_SUPPLEMENTAL <- TRUE

# Set FORCE_REFIT to TRUE only when data, features, folds, or tuning grids change.
FORCE_REFIT <- FALSE
OUTPUT_DIR <- "Model Outputs"
dir.create(OUTPUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

cached_result <- function(path, expression, force_refit = FORCE_REFIT) {
  if (file.exists(path) && !force_refit) return(readRDS(path))
  value <- base::force(expression)
  saveRDS(value, path)
  value
}

package_versions <- data.frame(
  package = required_modeling_packages(),
  version = vapply(required_modeling_packages(), function(x) {
    as.character(utils::packageVersion(x))
  }, character(1))
)
kable(package_versions, caption = "Modeling package versions")
```

The seed, folds, and thread count are declared once. Intermediate results are
cached so the document can be rendered repeatedly without refitting unchanged
models. Four threads provide a practical balance between speed and leaving the
computer responsive.

::: {.callout-note title="Runtime and cached results"}
The first complete run is intentionally the slowest because it builds historical
aggregates and cross-validates every candidate. Later renders reuse files in
`Model Outputs`. Set `FORCE_REFIT <- TRUE` only after changing the data, folds,
features, or tuning grids.
:::

## 2. Load application and historical data

```{r}
#| label: load-data

train_raw <- read_csv("application_train.csv", show_col_types = FALSE,
                      progress = FALSE)
test_raw <- read_csv("application_test.csv", show_col_types = FALSE,
                     progress = FALSE)

if (USE_SUPPLEMENTAL) {
  enriched <- load_or_build_enriched_applications(
    train_raw, test_raw,
    cache_path = file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "enriched_applications.rds")
  )
  train_source <- enriched$train
  test_source <- enriched$test
  feature_source <- "Application and supplemental history"
} else {
  train_source <- train_raw
  test_source <- test_raw
  feature_source <- "Application data only"
}

data_inventory <- data.frame(
  data = c("Training", "Test"),
  rows = c(nrow(train_source), nrow(test_source)),
  columns = c(ncol(train_source), ncol(test_source)),
  target_available = c("Yes", "No"),
  feature_source = feature_source
)
kable(data_inventory, caption = "Modeling data inventory")
```

Historical tables contain multiple records per applicant. The preparation
script filters them to pre-application information, aggregates each table to one
row per `SK_ID_CURR`, and then joins those summaries without changing the
application-table grain. The original test row order is preserved for the final
submission.

## 3. Engineer candidate predictors

```{r}
#| label: feature-engineering

train_model <- make_modeling_frame(train_source)
test_model <- make_modeling_frame(test_source)

predictor_names <- setdiff(names(train_model), c("SK_ID_CURR", "TARGET"))
stopifnot(identical(predictor_names,
                    setdiff(names(test_model), "SK_ID_CURR")))

feature_audit <- data.frame(
  measure = c(
    "Training rows", "Test rows", "Candidate predictors",
    "Numeric predictors", "Categorical predictors",
    "Predictors containing missing values"
  ),
  value = c(
    nrow(train_model), nrow(test_model), length(predictor_names),
    sum(vapply(train_model[predictor_names], is.numeric, logical(1))),
    sum(!vapply(train_model[predictor_names], is.numeric, logical(1))),
    sum(vapply(train_model[predictor_names], anyNA, logical(1)))
  )
)
kable(feature_audit, caption = "Feature-engineering audit")
```

The engineered predictors retain the original application fields and add
interpretable measures such as age, employment tenure, credit-to-income,
annuity-to-income, external-score summaries, missingness flags, and aggregated
credit-history behavior. `SK_ID_CURR` is retained only for row identification
and is never supplied to a model.

```{r}
#| label: missingness-review

missingness <- data.frame(
  predictor = predictor_names,
  missing_rate = vapply(train_model[predictor_names], function(x) {
    mean(is.na(x) | (is.numeric(x) & !is.finite(x)))
  }, numeric(1))
) |>
  arrange(desc(missing_rate)) |>
  slice_head(n = 15)

kable(missingness, digits = 3,
      caption = "Predictors with the most missing information")
```

Missing values are not automatically treated as noise. The linear and tree
benchmarks use analysis-fold medians plus explicit numeric missingness flags.
XGBoost compares this approach with native missing-value routing, which learns
the preferred branch for a missing value at each split.

::: {.callout-tip title="Why native missing-value handling is tested"}
Missingness was associated with `TARGET` during EDA. XGBoost's native routing
can preserve that signal without inventing a median value, while the explicit
comparison below determines whether it actually improves held-out AUC.
:::

## 4. Create and verify fixed cross-validation folds

```{r}
#| label: cross-validation-folds

fold_path <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "fixed_stratified_folds.rds")
if (file.exists(fold_path) && !FORCE_REFIT) {
  fold_id <- readRDS(fold_path)
  if (length(fold_id) != nrow(train_model)) {
    stop("Cached folds do not match the current training row count. Set FORCE_REFIT = TRUE.")
  }
} else {
  fold_id <- make_stratified_folds(train_model$TARGET, CV_FOLDS, SEED)
  saveRDS(fold_id, fold_path)
}

fold_audit <- fold_balance_table(train_model$TARGET, fold_id)
kable(fold_audit, digits = 4,
      caption = "Fixed stratified cross-validation folds")
```

Each row appears in one assessment fold and four analysis folds. Stratification
keeps the event rate nearly identical across folds, making AUC comparisons more
stable. These stored fold assignments are reused for every experiment below.

## 5. Establish benchmark models

### Null model

```{r}
#| label: null-model

null_results <- cross_validate_null(train_model, fold_id)
null_summary <- summarize_cv_results(null_results)
kable(null_summary, digits = 4, caption = "Null-model cross-validation results")
```

The null model assigns the analysis-fold event rate to every assessment row. Its
ROC AUC is 0.50 by construction. It is a probability-error reference rather
than a useful ranking model.

### Elastic-net logistic regression

```{r}
#| label: elastic-net

glmnet_grid <- default_glmnet_grid()
kable(glmnet_grid, caption = "Elastic-net tuning grid")

glmnet_results <- cached_result(
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "cv_glmnet.rds"),
  cross_validate_glmnet(train_model, fold_id, glmnet_grid)
)
glmnet_summary <- summarize_cv_results(glmnet_results)
kable(slice_head(glmnet_summary, n = 6), digits = 4,
      caption = "Leading elastic-net configurations")
```

Elastic-net logistic regression is the main interpretable benchmark. `alpha =
1` applies lasso shrinkage, while `alpha = 0.5` combines lasso and ridge
shrinkage. A pure ridge path was excluded after a full-data timing check showed
that it was disproportionately slow for this notebook. Shrinkage remains
important because dummy encoding and feature engineering create correlated
predictors.

### Pruned decision tree

```{r}
#| label: decision-tree

tree_grid <- default_tree_grid()
tree_results <- cached_result(
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "cv_decision_tree.rds"),
  cross_validate_decision_tree(train_model, fold_id, tree_grid)
)
tree_summary <- summarize_cv_results(tree_results)
kable(tree_summary, digits = 4,
      caption = "Pruned decision-tree configurations")
```

The single tree is intentionally shallow and uses a compact set of EDA-relevant
features. It provides an understandable nonlinear benchmark, though an ensemble
is expected to rank applicants more accurately.

### Random forest

```{r}
#| label: random-forest

forest_results <- cached_result(
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "cv_xgboost_forest.rds"),
  cross_validate_xgboost_forest(
    train_model, fold_id, trees = 100L, max_depth = 8L, nthread = NTHREAD
  )
)
forest_summary <- summarize_cv_results(forest_results)
kable(forest_summary, digits = 4,
      caption = "Random-forest cross-validation results")
```

The forest uses XGBoost's independent-tree mode. This retains random-forest
behavior while fitting the full dataset much faster than the legacy R
`randomForest` engine.

## 6. Tune gradient-boosted trees and missing-value treatment

```{r}
#| label: xgboost-grid

xgb_grid <- default_xgboost_grid()
kable(xgb_grid, caption = "Initial XGBoost tuning grid")

xgb_results <- cached_result(
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "cv_xgboost_initial.rds"),
  cross_validate_xgboost(
    train_model, fold_id, xgb_grid,
    nthread = NTHREAD, early_stopping_rounds = 30L
  )
)
xgb_summary <- summarize_cv_results(xgb_results)
kable(xgb_summary, digits = 4,
      caption = "XGBoost tuning and missing-data comparison")
```

The grid varies tree depth, learning rate, child-size regularization, and
missing-data treatment. Early stopping ends a fold when additional trees stop
improving its assessment AUC, limiting both overfitting and runtime. Comparing
native missing routing with median imputation directly tests which treatment is
more effective on this dataset.

```{r}
#| label: xgboost-refinement

# If the leading configuration reaches its tree cap in every fold, extend only
# that configuration. This is much cheaper than expanding the entire grid.
best_initial_xgb <- slice_head(xgb_summary, n = 1)
refinement_grid <- data.frame(
  max_depth = best_initial_xgb$max_depth,
  eta = best_initial_xgb$eta,
  min_child_weight = best_initial_xgb$min_child_weight,
  subsample = best_initial_xgb$subsample,
  colsample_bytree = best_initial_xgb$colsample_bytree,
  numeric_imputation = best_initial_xgb$numeric_imputation,
  class_weight = "none",
  nrounds = max(500L, as.integer(ceiling(best_initial_xgb$best_iteration_mean * 1.5)))
)

refinement_results <- cached_result(
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "cv_xgboost_refinement.rds"),
  cross_validate_xgboost(
    train_model, fold_id, refinement_grid,
    nthread = NTHREAD, early_stopping_rounds = 30L
  )
)
refinement_summary <- summarize_cv_results(refinement_results)
kable(refinement_summary, digits = 4,
      caption = "Focused XGBoost tree-count refinement")
```

The refinement extends only the best initial structure. It determines whether
the original tree cap stopped a still-improving model without multiplying every
other hyperparameter combination.

## 7. Test class-imbalance strategies

```{r}
#| label: imbalance-experiments

best_unweighted_xgb <- bind_rows(xgb_results, refinement_results) |>
  summarize_cv_results() |>
  slice_head(n = 1)
imbalance_grid <- data.frame(
  max_depth = best_unweighted_xgb$max_depth,
  eta = best_unweighted_xgb$eta,
  min_child_weight = best_unweighted_xgb$min_child_weight,
  subsample = best_unweighted_xgb$subsample,
  colsample_bytree = best_unweighted_xgb$colsample_bytree,
  numeric_imputation = best_unweighted_xgb$numeric_imputation,
  class_weight = c("sqrt", "balanced"),
  # Keep the same tree budget as the unweighted winner so this experiment
  # isolates the effect of class weighting.
  nrounds = as.integer(round(best_unweighted_xgb$best_iteration_mean))
)
kable(imbalance_grid, caption = "Class-weight experiments")

imbalance_results <- cached_result(
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "cv_xgboost_imbalance_refined.rds"),
  cross_validate_xgboost(
    train_model, fold_id, imbalance_grid,
    nthread = NTHREAD, early_stopping_rounds = 30L
  )
)

xgb_all_results <- bind_rows(xgb_results, refinement_results, imbalance_results)
xgb_all_summary <- summarize_cv_results(xgb_all_results)
kable(xgb_all_summary, digits = 4,
      caption = "XGBoost results including class weighting")
```

Class weights change how strongly the model penalizes errors on `TARGET = 1`.
The square-root strategy is moderate; the balanced strategy uses the full ratio
of non-events to events. Weighting is retained only if it improves
cross-validated ranking. Synthetic oversampling is not used because tree models
already learn nonlinear boundaries, it adds substantial runtime, and it can
distort probability calibration.

## 8. Compare all candidate models

```{r}
#| label: model-comparison

comparison <- bind_rows(
  null_summary,
  glmnet_summary,
  tree_summary,
  forest_summary,
  xgb_all_summary
) |>
  select(model, config, roc_auc_mean, roc_auc_sd,
         pr_auc_mean, pr_auc_sd, brier_mean, brier_sd, folds) |>
  arrange(desc(roc_auc_mean))

kable(comparison, digits = 4,
      caption = "Cross-validated candidate-model comparison")

ggplot(comparison, aes(x = reorder(paste(model, config, sep = ": "), roc_auc_mean),
                       y = roc_auc_mean, color = model)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = roc_auc_mean - roc_auc_sd,
                    ymax = roc_auc_mean + roc_auc_sd), width = 0.15) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Cross-validated ROC AUC by model configuration",
    x = NULL, y = "Mean ROC AUC (error bar = one fold SD)", color = "Model"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The winning configuration is selected by mean fold ROC AUC. Fold standard
deviation is shown so a very small apparent advantage can be interpreted in the
context of resampling variability.

## 9. Diagnose the selected model

```{r}
#| label: selected-model

best_xgb <- slice_head(xgb_all_summary, n = 1)
best_model_record <- best_xgb |>
  mutate(
    selected_on = Sys.Date(),
    selection_metric = "Five-fold cross-validated ROC AUC",
    external_test_auc = NA_real_,
    external_test_status = "Pending competition submission"
  )

write_csv(best_model_record,
          file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "best_model_score_record.csv"))
kable(best_model_record, digits = 4,
      caption = "Selected model and recorded validation score")
```

The recorded score is an internal out-of-fold estimate. The supplied test file
has no `TARGET`, so its AUC cannot be calculated locally. An external competition
score should be entered in the record only after submitting the prediction file.

::: {.callout-warning title="CV AUC is not the hidden test AUC"}
The notebook can calculate cross-validated AUC because `TARGET` is available for
training rows. The competition test outcomes are hidden, so the true test AUC
can only be recorded after the generated submission is scored externally.
:::

```{r}
#| label: calibration

selected_grid <- data.frame(
  max_depth = best_xgb$max_depth,
  eta = best_xgb$eta,
  min_child_weight = best_xgb$min_child_weight,
  subsample = best_xgb$subsample,
  colsample_bytree = best_xgb$colsample_bytree,
  numeric_imputation = best_xgb$numeric_imputation,
  class_weight = best_xgb$class_weight,
  nrounds = max(100L, as.integer(round(best_xgb$best_iteration_mean)))
)

oof_predictions <- cached_result(
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "selected_xgboost_oof_predictions_refined.rds"),
  cross_validated_xgboost_predictions(
    train_model, fold_id, selected_grid, nthread = NTHREAD
  )
)

selected_oof_metrics <- score_probabilities(
  oof_predictions$truth, oof_predictions$probability
)
calibration <- calibration_table(
  oof_predictions$truth, oof_predictions$probability
)

kable(selected_oof_metrics, digits = 4,
      caption = "Selected model pooled out-of-fold metrics")
kable(calibration, digits = 4,
      caption = "Out-of-fold calibration by predicted-risk decile")

ggplot(calibration, aes(x = predicted, y = observed)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), color = "#2C7FB8") +
  geom_line(color = "#2C7FB8") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "Selected-model calibration",
       x = "Mean predicted probability", y = "Observed TARGET rate",
       size = "Applications") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

Pooled out-of-fold predictions give each training application a probability from
a model that did not train on that application. The calibration table compares
mean predicted risk with the observed event rate across ten equally populated
risk bands. This diagnostic complements AUC, which measures ordering but not the
accuracy of probability levels.

## 10. Refit and create test probabilities

```{r}
#| label: final-fit

final_fit <- cached_result(
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "final_xgboost_fit.rds"),
  fit_final_xgboost(
    train_model, test_model, best_xgb,
    final_nrounds = max(1L, as.integer(round(best_xgb$best_iteration_mean))),
    nthread = NTHREAD
  )
)

submission_path <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "home_credit_submission.csv")
write_csv(final_fit$submission, submission_path)

submission_audit <- data.frame(
  measure = c(
    "Rows", "Unique applicant IDs", "Missing probabilities",
    "Minimum probability", "Mean probability", "Maximum probability",
    "Trees used in final fit"
  ),
  value = c(
    nrow(final_fit$submission),
    dplyr::n_distinct(final_fit$submission$SK_ID_CURR),
    sum(is.na(final_fit$submission$TARGET)),
    min(final_fit$submission$TARGET),
    mean(final_fit$submission$TARGET),
    max(final_fit$submission$TARGET),
    final_fit$nrounds
  )
)
kable(submission_audit, digits = 5,
      caption = "Final test-prediction validation")

head(final_fit$submission)
```

The selected workflow is refit on all labeled applications. Its number of trees
is the mean best iteration from cross-validation, which transfers the stopping
decision without using the unlabeled test data. The final file preserves every
test applicant ID and contains a bounded `TARGET` probability with no missing
values.

## 11. Final conclusion

```{r}
#| label: conclusion-values

cat(sprintf(
  paste0(
    "The selected model is %s (%s). Its mean five-fold ROC AUC is %.4f ",
    "with a fold standard deviation of %.4f. The submission file is %s."
  ),
  best_xgb$model, best_xgb$config,
  best_xgb$roc_auc_mean, best_xgb$roc_auc_sd,
  submission_path
))
```

The cross-validated AUC above is the final locally measurable score. The
competition test AUC remains unknown until the submission file is evaluated
against hidden outcomes. Once available, that external score should be added to
`best_model_score_record.csv` without replacing the cross-validation result.
